title: BUN (Blood Urea Nitrogen)
attribution: Source: MedlinePlus, National Library of Medicine.
measures: Measures urea nitrogen, a waste product from protein breakdown, in the blood. It helps check kidney function and can help find kidney problems early, and is often part of a metabolic panel.
low: Lower-than-usual levels may be linked to a lack of protein in the diet, malnutrition or liver disease.
high: Higher-than-usual levels may be caused by dehydration, burns, certain medicines, a high-protein diet or a recent heart attack. In general a high level may mean the kidneys are not working well.
notes: Normal levels vary by sex and usually rise with age. BUN is only one measure of kidney function, so other tests such as creatinine or GFR may be needed.
